name: Battle of Plassey
note: The accounts give no compass directions, so the plan is laid out with the river at the left and the Nawab's entrenchments at the top; distances are not to scale. The turning of the entrenchment, the two tanks, the lodge and the hill are placed from the distances the accounts give. The accounts do not say in which direction the French and the Nawab's other troops retreated; the retreats are drawn towards the entrenchment and away from the British.

terrain.name: Bhagirathi River
terrain.quote: Its length was angled diagonally to the Bhagirathi River.

terrain.name: Laksha Bagh
terrain.quote: They quickly occupied the adjoining mango grove, called Laksha Bagh

terrain.name: Hunting lodge
terrain.quote: a hunting lodge enclosed by a masonry wall where Clive took up his quarters

terrain.name: Nawab's entrenchments
terrain.quote: Their army lay behind earthen entrenchments running at right angles to the river for 200 yards

terrain.name: Redoubt
terrain.quote: There was a redoubt mounted by cannon at this turning along the entrenchment.

terrain.name: Small hill
terrain.quote: There was a small hill covered by trees 300 yards (270 m) east of the redoubt.

terrain.name: Small tank
terrain.quote: 800 yards (730 m) towards the British position was a small tank (reservoir), and 100 yards (91 m) further south was a larger tank

terrain.name: Larger tank
terrain.quote: 800 yards (730 m) towards the British position was a small tank (reservoir), and 100 yards (91 m) further south was a larger tank

units.name: British left sepoys
units.quote: The sepoys were placed on the right and left in equal divisions.

units.name: British Europeans, centre
units.quote: The Europeans and Topasses were placed in the centre of the line in four divisions

units.name: British right sepoys
units.quote: The sepoys were placed on the right and left in equal divisions.

units.name: British guns at the kilns
units.quote: Clive posted two 6-pounders and two howitzers behind some brick kilns 200 yards (180 m) north of the left division of his army to oppose the French fire.

units.name: Kilpatrick's detachment
units.quote: he took two companies of the 39th Regiment and two field pieces and advanced towards St. Frais' position

units.name: Grant's three platoons
units.quote: sent three platoons under Captain Grant and Lieutenant Rumbold and a field piece under John Johnstone

units.name: Coote's grenadiers
units.quote: Two companies of grenadiers of the 39th Regiment, under Major Coote, took the hill at 16:30

units.name: French artillery
units.quote: The French took up positions at the larger tank with four light pieces advanced by two larger pieces

units.name: Mir Madan Khan's body
units.quote: Behind them was a body of 5,000 cavalry and 7,000 infantry commanded by the Nawab's faithful general Mir Madan Khan

units.name: Nawab's right, Rai Durlabh
units.quote: The right arm of their army was commanded by Rai Durlabh, the centre by Yar Lutuf Khan and the left arm closest to the British by Mir Jafar.

units.name: Nawab's centre, Yar Lutuf
units.quote: The right arm of their army was commanded by Rai Durlabh, the centre by Yar Lutuf Khan and the left arm closest to the British by Mir Jafar.

units.name: Nawab's left, Mir Jafar
units.quote: The right arm of their army was commanded by Rai Durlabh, the centre by Yar Lutuf Khan and the left arm closest to the British by Mir Jafar.

phases.title: The two armies take their ground
phases.text: The Nawab's army formed an arc with the French guns at the larger tank in front. Clive lined up the Europeans in the centre with a sepoy division on each side, and posted four guns at the kilns to answer the French.
phases.quote: The Europeans and Topasses were placed in the centre of the line in four divisions, flanked on both sides by three 6-pounders.

phases.title: The guns open and Clive withdraws to the grove
phases.text: The French guns fired the first shot and the rest of the Nawab's artillery followed. The British lost 10 Europeans and 20 sepoys by 8:30, and Clive left the advanced guns at the kilns and drew the army back into the grove.
phases.quote: Leaving the advanced artillery at the brick kilns, Clive ordered the army to retreat to the relative shelter of the grove.

phases.title: Rain, and Mir Madan Khan's charge is driven back
phases.text: A rainstorm drenched the Nawab's gunpowder, while the British covered theirs. Mir Madan Khan led his cavalry in a charge, but British grapeshot mortally wounded him and drove his men back.
phases.quote: As the rain began to subside, Mir Madan Khan, assuming that the British guns were rendered ineffective by the rain, led his cavalry to a charge.

phases.title: The Nawab's army turns back to its entrenchments
phases.text: The Nawab's army stopped its cannonade and began turning back north to its entrenchments. This left St. Frais and his artillery without support.
phases.quote: At about 14:00, the Nawab's army ceased the cannonade and began turning back north to their entrenchments, leaving St. Frais and his artillery without support.

phases.title: Kilpatrick advances on his own
phases.text: Seeing the Nawab’s forces retire, Major Kilpatrick, left in charge while Clive rested in the hunting lodge, took two companies and two field pieces and advanced towards St. Frais’ position.
phases.quote: he took two companies of the 39th Regiment and two field pieces and advanced towards St. Frais' position

phases.title: Clive leads the army against the French position
phases.text: Clive hurried to the detachment and had Kilpatrick bring up the rest of the army from the grove. He then led the army against St. Frais, whose artillery retreated to the redoubt of the entrenchment.
phases.quote: Clive himself then led the army against St. Frais' position, which was taken at 15:00 when the French artillery retreated to the redoubt of the entrenchment

phases.title: Mir Jafar's division turns towards the grove and is halted
phases.text: The Nawab's left arm, which had lingered behind the rest, turned and marched towards the grove. Clive took it for a threat to his baggage and sent three platoons and a field piece, whose fire halted it.
phases.quote: The fire of the field piece halted the advance of the division, which remained isolated from the rest of the Nawab's army.

phases.title: The British cannonade the camp from the larger tank
phases.text: British field pieces cannonaded the Nawab’s camp from the mound of the larger tank, and many of his troops and guns came out of the entrenchment. Clive moved half his troops and guns to the smaller tank and half to rising ground.
phases.quote: Meanwhile, the British field pieces began a cannonade on the Nawab's camp from the mound of the larger tank.

phases.title: The British take the hill and the redoubt
phases.text: Clive ordered a three-pronged attack on the redoubt and the hill east of it. Major Coote’s grenadiers took the hill at 16:30 after the enemy fled without firing a shot, and the redoubt fell after St. Frais was forced to retreat.
phases.quote: Clive ordered a three-pronged attack with simultaneous attacks by two detachments on the redoubt and the hill supported by the main force in the centre.

phases.title: The British hold the entrenchment and the camp
phases.text: By 17:00 the British occupied the entrenchment and the camp left by a dispersing army. The Nawab’s divisions broke up and left the field.
phases.quote: By 17:00, the British occupied the entrenchment and the camp left by a dispersing army.
